lessons.title: Lesson 1: LLMs vs Agents

video.title: What are AI agents? AI Agents Explained in 2 minutes
video.purpose: Quick visual intro to agents before CJ examples.

lessons.goal: Reagan can explain the difference between an LLM and an agent in normal words, using CJ examples instead of hype.
sections: Warm up
Write this in your own words: what is the difference between an AI that answers and an AI that acts?
Teach

An LLM is the brain. It predicts, reasons, writes, summarizes, and explains. Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are LLMs. An agent uses an LLM plus tools, memory, rules, and a goal. The simple line: an LLM thinks and answers. An agent thinks and acts.
Watch with purpose
Watch the IBM agent video. Write down the first moment where the video moves from talking to doing.
Build
Make a two column chart. Left side: LLM. Right side: agent. Add 5 examples to each side from CJ's world.
Submit
Submit your chart and a 4 sentence explanation of why CJ uses agents instead of only chatbots.

quiz.q: What is the cleanest difference between an LLM and an agent?
choices: An LLM answers, an agent can act with tools
They are the exact same thing

quiz.q: Which one is an LLM?
Which example fits an agent best?
choices: Explain what a press release is
Search Drive, find a file, update a project, and report proof

lessons.checkpoint: I can explain LLM vs agent without hype.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Claude Setup and First Prompt

video.title: Getting started with Claude.ai
video.purpose: Set up Claude, log in, and understand the first clicks without a long tutorial.

lessons.goal: Reagan creates or logs into Claude and runs a useful first prompt.
sections: Warm up
Claude is where you go when you need a smart thinking partner. It is strong for writing, planning, summarizing, and explaining.
Setup
Go to claude.ai. Create or log into your account. Confirm you can start a new chat. Do not add private passwords, tokens, or client info.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 5:19 Anthropic video. Pause after the first prompt example and write what made the prompt clear.
Build
Ask Claude to create a 5 step plan for setting up your AI workspace for this course. Then ask it to make the plan shorter and more direct.
Submit
Submit a screenshot showing Claude open and paste the final 5 step plan into your workbook.

quiz.q: What is Claude best used for in this course?
What should you avoid pasting into Claude?
What makes a first prompt useful?
choices: Context, goal, constraints, and desired output

sections: Warm up
Codex is for building, editing, reviewing, and checking work. Think of it as another smart teammate, not a magic button.
Setup

Watch with purpose

Build

Submit
Submit a screenshot showing Codex access and 3 bullets on when you would choose Codex instead of Claude.

sections: Warm up
Telegram is the front door. The agent is the worker behind it. BotFather creates the bot account, then Hermes connects the bot to the agent.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 1:34 BotFather clip. Write down what BotFather creates and what it does not create.
Setup
Create the Telegram bot with BotFather. Save the bot name. Do not paste the bot token into public docs or screenshots. CJ approves the token connection step.
Hermes connection
Follow the guided internal setup for the Telegram gateway. Confirm you can send one message to the bot and get one response back.
Proof
Submit a screenshot of the bot chat working, with any private token hidden. Add the bot name and the date to proof-log.md.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Markdown, Saved Work, Wiki, and Closeout

video.title: Markdown in 2 Minutes
video.purpose: Show Markdown as simple structured text before she builds workspace files.

lessons.goal: Reagan builds the habit of saving useful work in Markdown, backing it up, and closing the loop with proof.
sections: Markdown is the playbook
Markdown is plain text with structure. Use headings, bullets, links, screenshots, and checklists. It is how we keep work readable for people and useful for agents.
Karpathy style setup
Start every workspace with clear context, examples, constraints, and proof. The agent should not guess where things live or what good looks like.
Wiki and vaults

The wiki is where durable knowledge goes. Vaults split work by lane: main ops, QB Stable content, RISE content, Brady football knowledge, and recruiting. Rea does not need to master every vault yet. She needs to know that good knowledge gets saved where the team can find it.
Closeout habit
Every session ends with what changed, where it lives, proof, and the next step. If it is not written down, it did not happen.
Build
Create an ai-workspace folder with my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, and closeout.md. Add today’s setup notes and one clean next step.

quiz.q: What is Markdown best for here?
What belongs in a closeout note?
choices: What changed, where it lives, proof, and next step

quiz.q: Why use wiki and vaults?
choices: To save durable knowledge where the team can find it

quiz.q: What is the Karpathy style setup idea for Rea?
choices: Give the agent clear context, examples, constraints, and proof

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Skills, Commands, Tools, and MCPs

video.title: MCP Explained in 2 Minutes
video.purpose: Explain MCP as a connection standard in plain language.

lessons.goal: Reagan knows these building blocks can exist across Claude, Codex, and other agent systems.
sections: Warm up
A command tells the agent what to do. A skill is a saved best practice. A tool lets the agent touch the outside world. An MCP is a clean way to connect tools and data.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 2:28 MCP clip. Write down the simplest definition of MCP in one sentence.
Examples we actually use
Closeout is a skill. Wiki is durable memory. Drive backup protects files. Telegram is an access point. MCPs connect agents to systems when the setup supports it.
Best practice
Do not teach random frameworks just because they are popular. Use the system CJ actually runs. If we do not use it, it does not belong in Setup 101.
Build
Add a glossary to my-ai-workspace.md with: LLM, agent, command, skill, tool, MCP, wiki, vault, closeout, Drive backup.

quiz.q: Are skills and commands tied to one app only?
choices: Yes, only one app has them
No, similar ideas can exist across multiple agent systems

quiz.q: What is an MCP?
choices: A standard connection that lets an agent use outside tools or data

quiz.q: What should Reagan ask when a term appears in a new app?
choices: What app am I using, and what does this word mean here?

lessons.checkpoint: I can explain the building blocks without thinking they belong to only one tool.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: First Project, My AI Workspace

video.title: How To Use Google Drive
video.purpose: Show the backup habit for files, screenshots, and proof.

lessons.goal: Reagan finishes with a real AI workspace, saved progress, a Drive backup, and a clear resume point.
sections: Project brief
Build My AI Workspace. It should prove she can log into Claude, use Codex, message the Telegram agent, save Markdown notes, and back up proof.
Progress save
Use the Save progress button in this course. Download the progress file. Upload it to the AI Workspace folder in Google Drive.
Drive backup
Back up my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, closeout.md, and screenshots to Drive. The rule is simple: local work plus cloud proof.
Closeout
Write one closeout note: what was set up, what worked, what is still missing, where the files live, and what the next step is.
Submit
Submit the Drive folder link or screenshot, the downloaded progress file, and the final closeout note.

quiz.q: What is the Week 1 project?
choices: Set up, save, and back up my AI workspace

quiz.q: What must Reagan be able to do later?
choices: Open the saved progress file, Drive folder, and closeout note

quiz.q: What makes the project complete?
choices: Working access, saved files, Drive backup, proof, and closeout

qualityRules: Every lesson must have at least one relevant visual aid: video, graphic, online image, docs card, X post, or useful combination.
Quiz correct answers must be varied. Do not make every correct answer A.
Prefer short YouTube clips over generic link cards when a credible short clip exists.
Do not teach tools or frameworks we do not use in CJ operations.
Every setup lesson must include a save, backup, and resume habit.
